brief.headline: Push them from ₹295/KG to ₹290/KG (matching Shrinath) and offer to pay 15 days faster in return — they're loss-making and cash-tight, so faster payment is valuable to them.

priceAsk.summary: Match Shrinath's ₹290/KG on all three laminate SKUs
priceAsk.basis: We already pay Shrinath Roto Pack Pvt Ltd ₹290.00/KG for identical laminates; GLS charges ₹295.00/KG, a 1.7% gap. The market asking band for pharma ORS sachet laminate is ₹205–305/kg (typical ₹250/kg), so their price sits at the top of fair — matching our best price is completely justified.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days faster (45 days total instead of 30) in exchange for the ₹5/KG price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Costs us ₹9.49 L in cash (we pay sooner), but they borrow money at about 10.96%, so the 15 extra days are worth roughly that rate to them — a fair trade for the ₹5/KG saving.

brief.financialLeverage: GLS lost money in FY2024-25 (₹-23.68 Cr) and scores only 2/10 on money-health — they're fragile. They owe 2.15 times their own cash (₹208.21 Cr total debt) and their interest bill eats nearly all their operating profit (0.06x coverage). We're a tiny customer (0.33% of their ₹691.05 Cr revenue), so we can't squeeze hard without risking supply. Lead with the faster-payment swap: their cash is stuck for 49 days (better than similar firms at 61d, but still tight given the losses), and they borrow at about 10.96%, so earlier payment has real value. Frame it as helping them while getting us to Shrinath's price — not a hard discount demand.

evidence.point: We pay ₹5/KG more than our cheapest supplier for the same laminates
They owe more than twice their own cash

evidence.figure: 0.06x interest coverage — nearly all operating profit goes to interest

evidence.point: They borrow at a high rate

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter already supplying FDC in small volume — proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets (₹2755.75 Cr revenue, C health 58/100).

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant doing both film and conversion — can handle ORS sachets at scale (₹16492.00 Cr revenue, C health 46/100).

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter specializing in pharma blister and sachet laminates — strong fit for Electral (₹222.04 Cr revenue, D health 31/100).

risks: They're loss-making and fragile (2/10 money-health, IVR BBB- rating, five red flags including severe legal cases, GST and EPF delays) — pushing too hard could tip them over and disrupt our Electral supply.
We're only 0.33% of their revenue, so we have little leverage by size — the ask must rest on the Shrinath benchmark and the payment-speed trade, not on volume clout.
Their Altman Z-score is 1.68 (grey zone, between healthy and distressed) — not in immediate danger, but watch for any worsening signs quarter-to-quarter.
If they reject the ₹290/KG match, be ready to shift more volume to Shrinath or qualify Huhtamaki/Constantia fast — don't get stuck paying the premium with no Plan B.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to match the ₹290/KG we pay Shrinath on these three laminates — and to help your cash flow, we can move to 45-day payment instead of 30 if that works for you.
